allocation_status: Teaching design; source gives no official allocation.
rationale: Twelve 40-minute lessons separate family definitions and sorting all20 elements,physical evidence,three source-named reaction contexts,comparison,metal and noble-gas uses,daily uses,road-safety reasoning and an independent final. Paper reaction records are an explicit adaptation,not a performed chemical investigation. Actual source practical and digital activities need approved provision.
prerequisites: First20 elements and groups,simple atom counts and balanced-equation notation.
Distinguish a given record from an actual observation.
teacher_confirmation_required: Clarify source transition examples Zn/Pb; teach the stated scientific definition and preserve verbatim source.
No learner sodium,chlorine or lead handling,chemical mixing,gas generation,flames or mains electricity. A separate qualified risk assessment is needed for any actual chemical investigation.
CF3 known clean Cu/steel physical option needs approved specimens,a safe circuit and training; otherwise record actual investigation not performed.
Source chemical investigation and first-aid use are not certified by supplied records; retain unperformed status pending an approved actual opportunity.
Any actual demonstration requires a current qualified protocol and school approval; this pack supplies none.
Preview digital sources and record actual use; print notes are not digital performance.
Confirm access,pacing,road-safety discussion and observed care actions.

lesson_map.title: Which family definition fits the evidence?
Where do all first twenty elements belong?
What physical properties can be investigated safely?
How do magnesium conditions change a record?
When is a reaction comparison not applicable?
How can records be compared fairly?
How do named metals relate to uses?
How can unreactive gases be useful?
Why distinguish an element from its compounds?
Can family,property and use claims be defended?
